The CABT Exam and How This Course Works

Unit 1: Welcome to Healthcare Technology Management. Lesson 2 of 53 in BMET Academy.

You are studying for one specific test, so it pays to know exactly what it looks like before you study a single fact. Here is the exam, then here is the path this course walks you down.

The exam

The CABT, the Certified Associate in Biomedical Technology, is the entry-level credential from ACI, the credentials institute inside AAMI. It is:

Questions      100 multiple choice
Time           2 hours, closed book, nothing on the desk
Delivery       live remote proctoring, year-round: webcam, microphone, quiet room
Eligibility    high school junior or above; no degree and no experience required
Fee            $220 member, $270 non-member, non-refundable
Window         six months from purchase to the day you test
Retake         $190 member, $240 non-member, after a 60-day wait
Result         pass or fail on the screen immediately
Validity       5 years, non-renewable

Six domains divide the questions: Anatomy and Physiology 10%, Medical Devices as Related to Patient Care 23%, Safety in Healthcare 16%, Fundamentals of Electricity and Electronics 14%, Reasoning and Problem Solving 24%, and Healthcare Information Technology 13%. Reasoning and the device domain together are nearly half the test, which is why so much of this course asks you to decide something rather than recall it.

Two of those facts bite people. Non-renewable means the associate credential expires in five years and cannot be renewed, so plan your next exam inside that window. And the 60-day wait plus a new fee is the cost of walking in unprepared.

How this course works

The stages run in order, and each one unlocks the next.

  1. The memorization sheet. Numbers, ranges, limits, and formulas. Read it first, on day one, before you understand any of it. The rest of the course keeps pointing back at it.
  2. The starter test. A short test that finds out what you already know and suggests where to begin.
  3. The tutorial. The lessons, unit by unit, each with a deeper explanation behind it, five or more questions, and a checkpoint at the end of the unit. Some lessons carry a hands-on lab.
  4. The 50-question test. Half the length of the real exam, 60 minutes, graded at 80% here because you train above the line, not at it.
  5. Retraining. Every topic you miss comes back as a short drill, a lesson to reread, or an extended set of questions.
  6. Practice tests until 3 of your last 5 reach 80%.
  7. The official-format test: 100 questions in 120 minutes, scored at the real exam's 70%. Pass it once and that pass is permanent.
  8. Ready. The certificate of completion needs all three: every lesson finished, every lab finished, and the official-format test passed.
Tip: the exam gives you an on-screen four-function calculator and nothing else. Practice the arithmetic in this course without a phone so the real thing feels normal.
Remember
CABT: 100 questions, 2 hours, closed book, remote proctored year-round, high school junior or above. $220 member and $270 non-member, retake $190 and $240 after a 60-day wait, six months to test, pass or fail immediately, valid 5 years and non-renewable. Course path: sheet, starter test, lessons and labs, 50-question test, retraining, practice until 3 of the last 5 hit 80%, then the official-format test at 70%.
Deeper explanation

The CABT Exam and How This Course Works, explained slowly

Buying and sitting the exam

The process is short, and the deadlines are the part people trip over.

  1. You apply and pay. Eligibility is high school junior or above, which means there is no degree requirement and no experience requirement standing between you and this credential.
  2. From the day of purchase you have six months to test. The fee is non-refundable, so do not buy it until you intend to study.
  3. You schedule a session. Delivery is live remote proctoring, year-round, so you test at your own computer with a human watching through the webcam. Expect to show identification, pan the camera around the room, clear the desk, and stay in frame; a phone, a second screen, notes, or somebody walking in can end the session.
  4. The exam is 100 multiple-choice questions in 2 hours, closed book, with an on-screen four-function calculator provided.
  5. You get pass or fail immediately on the screen, with written confirmation by email.
  6. If it goes badly, a retake costs less but waits 60 days.

The money and the calendar

Item                     Member    Non-member
First attempt            $220      $270
Retake                   $190      $240
Window to test           six months from purchase
Retake wait              60 days
Validity                 5 years, non-renewable

Those numbers argue for one thing: do not schedule the test until your practice scores say you are ready. A failed attempt costs the retake fee and two months of momentum.

Non-renewable, and what comes next

The associate credential cannot be renewed. In five years it simply expires, and the intent is that by then you have the work experience for the technician-level exam, CBET. That exam's full certification wants one of three things: an associate degree or higher in electronics, technology, or science plus two years of full-time biomedical equipment work; a United States military biomedical equipment program plus two years; or four years of that work on its own. Candidate status, which lets you sit it earlier, opens at the degree alone, the program alone, or two years of work alone. Read that as a plan, not a worry: pass this exam, get hired, log the years, and the next rung is already in reach.

Reading the domain weights as a study plan

Domain                                     Share   Questions out of 100
Reasoning and Problem Solving              24%     about 24
Medical Devices as Related to Patient Care 23%     about 23
Safety in Healthcare                       16%     about 16
Fundamentals of Electricity and Electronics 14%    about 14
Healthcare Information Technology          13%     about 13
Anatomy and Physiology                     10%     about 10

Reasoning is the largest single slice and it cannot be memorized. Those questions give you a situation and ask what you do first, what the reading means, or which cause to check next. That is why this course drills order-of-operations lists and why the labs make you decide something rather than just read a number.

How the gates in this course work

The 50-question tests and practice tests are scored at 80%, above the real cut, so your margin is real. Qualification needs 3 of your last 5 tests at 80% or better, which prevents one lucky run from sending you to the exam. After that comes the official-format test: 100 questions, 120 minutes, scored at the exam's own 70%. Pass it once and that pass is permanent. The certificate of completion needs every lesson finished, every lab finished, and that official-format pass.
